title: Failure Injection & Recovery Gate
scope: Local deterministic failure-injection and recovery proof across crash, power-loss, disk-full, permission-loss, missing-file, corrupt-index, and interrupted-migration scenarios on the canonical Windows repository. All evidence is synthetic/disposable (temp directories, in-memory or file-backed SQLite) or classified as native/operational gates that require interactive desktop or CI.

scenarios.metric: application crash produces a structured diagnostic and does not corrupt the last clean state
atomic rename sequence survives an interrupted rename with no data loss
scenarios.unit: survivors restored after simulated power-loss window

scenarios.metric: disk-full at the SQLite engine level is classified as a typed write-failure, not corruption
transient marker-delete permission failure does not propagate out of upsert or break project listing
scenarios.unit: transient delete errno does not destroy the package

scenarios.metric: missing manifest/project file is reported cleanly without crash
corrupt database file is detected by health/open paths without crashing
scenarios.unit: schemaVersion returns null on corrupt fixture; open throws typed

scenarios.metric: half-applied migration wave with stale user_version reopens cleanly and preserves Core rows
scenarios.unit: forward recovery on every entry v1..58 preserves data

baseline.profile: CrashDiagnostics writes structured JSON logs; StartupRecoveryPolicy decides normal/safe/recovery modes
atomicWrite rename sequence; registry/manifest survivors restored after interrupted rename
PRAGMA max_page_count injection; SQLITE_FULL (13) from engine classified as typed write failure
transient marker-delete errno stages via OS attrib/chmod; upsert completes; package not destroyed
ProjectOpenService returns typed failure for missing manifest/database
corrupt database fixture detected without crash; integrity_check and CorruptionScanReport
v1..58 entry versions forward-recover to current schema with Core rows preserved

bottlenecks.impact: Real process crash-dump capture and recovery dialog are exercised only via interactive desktop; cron cannot launch native crash flows.
bottlenecks.next_gate: Native computer-use journey on release-candidate hardware for crash dump + recovery dialog proof.

bottlenecks.impact: Power-loss proof is simulated via the rename-window injection, not actual hardware power-cut. True power-loss recovery requires physical device control.
bottlenecks.next_gate: Hands-on power-cut test with Choi on real hardware per 145.42.

bottlenecks.impact: Disk-full is proven at the SQLite engine level via PRAGMA max_page_count, not at the filesystem ENOSPC level on a real full volume.
bottlenecks.next_gate: Virtual volume ENOSPC injection in isolated media if a safe harness becomes available.

bottlenecks.impact: USB cold-eject and hot-reconnect behavior requires physical device action.

limits: All data-loss, recovery, and repair evidence is synthetic/disposable (temp directories, in-memory or file-backed SQLite via PRAGMA injection).
True hardware power-loss (actual power-cut) is not executed; proof is via rename-window crash simulation.
Volume-level ENOSPC (real full disk) is not executed; proof is via SQLite engine SQLITE_FULL injection.
Native GUI crash dialog, recovery prompt, and USB cold-eject/reinsert are UNVERIFIABLE from cron.
hosted CI, signing, hardware, and public release remain UNVERIFIABLE and belong to dedicated later gates.
This decision is not signing or public release approval.
